approach: I used the FE-03 procedure from the frontend-steps skill. First I read the contracted inputs: feat.tasks, feat.stories, feat.design and task.repo_access in full, and the frontend-relevant parts of feat.prd and feat.trd (IF-7, F-12 to F-14, T-12 to T-16, AC-19 to AC-21, NFR-3/7/10). Then I read the whole ap_portal checkout with Read and Glob: index.js, portal.test.js, package.json, ci.mjs, README.md and CLAUDE.md. That gave me the existing layer, exports, callers and CI rules. I mapped the TSK-07 / feat.design B4 components onto the single existing view-helper module and picked the smallest additive change. Everything stays in index.js: one new export, private helpers, two constants, a version step and new tests, with no new file or layer. The verifier subagent had checked the earlier content against its sources. In this rewrite I took out the unsupported statement about how the code was read and kept only facts the sources support. I did not use codegraph, because the repository is one small module plus one test file and I read all of it directly.

improvements: CQ-FE-1 (a missing or non-string id/vendor renders as the text 'undefined') is marked non-blocking because feat.design B4.2 gives an interim answer (String(value)). That reading is defensible. Still, it makes the person at the gate confirm on purpose that rendering 'undefined' is acceptable, instead of the agent settling it in FE-04.

The output says FC-8/FC-9 move VERSION 'one minor step from 2.3.0' and that the lane confirms the number. It could state the candidate value (2.4.0) as the proposal TK-07.5 asks for, marked as agent judgement and pending confirmation, so FE-04 has a concrete target.

'Minimum lines of code' is argued in words (one module, additive, no new file) but given no rough size. An approximate count of new lines per component, marked as agent judgement, would make the 'minimum' claim easier to check at the gate.
Section 5 says 'The table template is split across lines where needed'. That is a coding instruction rather than a component; it could be labelled agent judgement like the other design choices.
judge.notes:
I checked every statement in task.components.md against feat.tasks (TSK-07, section 2), feat.design (A1, A3, B4.1–B4.5, DD-1/3/5/8/11, SE-2/SE-4, HC-8/HC-9), feat.trd (F-12, F-13, IF-7.1–IF-7.9, T-12–T-16, TQ list), feat.stories (AC-07.1–AC-07.10, TK-07.5, SC-1), feat.prd (AC-19, NFR-10, OQ-B8–B10), task.repo_access (sections 1, 2, 4), and the ap_portal files (index.js, tests/portal.test.js, ci.mjs, package.json, CLAUDE.md, README.md, plus a file listing).

The code facts are accurate:
- VERSION 2.3.0 is set in both index.js and package.json.
- formatAmount uses Number(value || 0).toFixed(2).
- renderAgingSummary escapes nothing.
- The exports line is quoted correctly.
- formatAmount has no callers except renderAgingSummary and the tests.
- The two existing test names are quoted correctly.
- The CI rules (node --check, NODE_PATH=src, coverage >= 90 on src/**, the console\.log|\beval\( pattern, 140-character lines) match ci.mjs.
- The 'no stylesheet' claim matches the repository listing.

The other cited material also matches:
- The quote from ap_portal/CLAUDE.md is exact.
- The component list FC-1 to FC-10 matches the design's B4.1/B4.2 and the TSK-07 file budget.
- The traceability rows match the AC, IF and T numbers in the sources.
- The carried open questions and pending markers match feat.tasks and task.repo_access.

Design choices (header built from a constant, no new file) are marked as agent judgement. The statement that caused the earlier refusal, about a hook blocking shell commands, has been removed. The output fully meets the workbook outcome: it lists the components to create or update, keeps the change minimal and additive, and backs that up with sources.
